title: At most two chat engines alive, closed after five quiet minutes
request: Owner: the app is so huge when it runs; how can we make it better. Later: it is about runtime memory; yes, go on with fixes 1 and 2.
spec: dclab-code server/config.js (maxLiveEngines, idleCloseMinutes, RETIRED_DEFAULTS), server/engine.js (lastActive, resting), server/app.js (trimEngines)
plan: measure each process of the running app
check the tools server's import cost

decisions.decision: limit the number of live Claude Code processes (2) and close a quiet one after 5 minutes
decisions.why: measured: each chat holds its own process, 125 MB at rest and more while working, kept 20 minutes; the app and tools server together are a fixed 355 MB

decisions.decision: never close a process that is working, waiting for the person, rewinding or running a background job
decisions.why: closing those would lose an answer or kill a training run; a resting one resumes from its saved transcript

decisions.decision: a saved value equal to a retired default takes the new default
decisions.why: the first run saves every default, so the owner's config pinned 20 minutes and the change would never reach them

decisions.decision: fix 2 (lazy imports in R&D's tools server) not done
decisions.why: almost every DCLab tool reads a table, so pandas loads at the first tool call anyway: the 150 MB saving lasts minutes for a change across ~120 modules; stopping the whole server when idle saves 281 MB but it runs the job worker and every engine connects to it at start, so it needs job-aware restarts: proposed to the owner instead

findings.defect: the proposed lazy-import fix would barely help
findings.scenario: a DCLab chat calls home_status or get_results in its first turn
findings.cause: the tools read tables, so pandas, scikit-learn and pyarrow load at that call and stay
findings.fix: fix 2 dropped; the owner offered a job-aware stop of the idle tools server instead
findings.test: import trace: pandas via dclab_core.datacard <- contracts <- ledger <- tools; sklearn via expansion.runner <- studio.engine

findings.defect: a new default would not reach existing homes
findings.scenario: the owner's ~/.dclab-code/config.json holds idleCloseMinutes 20, saved by the first run
findings.cause: loadConfig lets every saved key win, and the first run saves the whole default config
findings.fix: RETIRED_DEFAULTS: a saved 20 gives way to 5; another chosen value stays
findings.test: server test: an old default saved in config.json gives way

measurements.name: memory at rest, before
measurements.result: app 73 MB, R&D tools server 281 MB (208 MB of it imports, 2.9 s), one Claude Code process 125 MB at rest

measurements.name: live: three real chats (Haiku 5.5)
measurements.gate: at most 2 processes after the third chat

outcome: Chat engines no longer pile up: two at most, a quiet one gone after five minutes, nothing lost.
lessons: Measure each process before proposing a memory fix: the growth was per chat, not the app.
A lazy import only helps if the first real use is rare; check what the first tool call loads.
When a first run saves every default, changing a default needs a migration for the saved copies.
risks: Reopening a chat closed after 5 minutes rebuilds its context; if the prompt cache expired, that turn costs a little more.
